来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Adults and children are frequently confronted with statements about the alarming rate of loss of tropical rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: For example, one graphic illustration to which children might readily relate is the estimate that rainforests are being destroyed at a rate equivalent to one thousand football fields every forty minutes - about the duration of a normal classroom period.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: In the face of the frequent and often vivid media coverage, it is likely that children will have formed ideas about rainforests - what and where they are, why they are important, what endangers them - independent of any formal tuition.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: It is also possible that some of these ideas will be mistaken.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Many studies have shown that children harbor misconceptions about 'pure', curriculum science.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: These misconceptions do not remain isolated but become incorporated into a multifaceted, but organized, conceptual framework, making it and the component ideas, some of which are erroneous, more robust but also accessible to modification.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: These ideas may be developed by children absorbing ideas through the popular media.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Sometimes this information may be erroneous.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: It seems schools may not be providing an opportunity for children to re-express their ideas and so have them tested and refined by teachers and their peers.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Despite the extensive coverage in the popular media of the destruction of rainforests, little formal information is available about children's ideas in this area.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The aim of the present study is to start to provide such information, to help teachers design their educational strategies to build upon correct ideas and to displace misconceptions and to plan programs in environmental studies in their schools.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The study surveys children's scientific knowledge and attitudes to rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Secondary school children were asked to complete a questionnaire containing five open-form questions.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The most frequent responses to the first question were descriptions which are self-evident from the term 'rainforest'.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some children described them as damp, wet or hot.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The second question concerned the geographical location of rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The commonest responses were continents or countries: Africa (given by 43% of children), South America (30%), Brazil (25%).

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some children also gave more general locations, such as being near the Equator.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Responses to question three concerned the importance of rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The dominant idea, raised by 64% of the pupils, was that rainforests provide animals with habitats.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Fewer students responded that rainforests provide plant habitats, and even fewer (60%) raised the idea of rainforest as animal habitats.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Similarly, but at a lower level, more girls (13%) than boys (5%) said that rainforests provided human habitats.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: These observations are generally consistent with our previous studies of pupils' views about the use and conservation of rainforests, in which girls were shown to be more sympathetic to animals and expressed views which seem to place an intrinsic value on non-human animal life.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The fourth question concerned the causes of the destruction of rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Perhaps encouragingly, more than half of the pupils (59%) identified that it is human activities which are destroying rainforests, some personalizing the responsibility by the use of terms such as 'we are'.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: About 18% of the pupils referred specifically to logging activity.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: One misconception, expressed by some 1% of the pupils, was that acid rain is responsible for rainforest destruction.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: A similar proportion said that pollution is destroying rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Here, children are confusing rainforest destruction with damage to the forests of Western Europe by these factors.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: While two fifths of the students provided the information that the rainforests provide oxygen, in some cases this response also embraced the misconception that rainforest destruction would reduce atmospheric oxygen, making the atmosphere incompatible with human life on Earth.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: In answer to the final question about the importance of rainforest conservation, the majority of children simply said that we need rainforests to survive.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Only a few of the pupils (6%) mentioned that rainforest destruction may contribute to global warming.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: This is surprising considering the high level of media coverage on this issue.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some children expressed the idea that the conservation of rainforests is not important.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: The results of this study suggest that certain ideas predominate in the thinking of children about rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Pupils' responses indicate some misconceptions in basic scientific knowledge of rainforests' ecosystems such as their ideas about rainforests as habitats for animals, plants and humans and the relationship between climatic change and destruction of rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Pupils did not volunteer ideas that suggested that they appreciated the complexity of causes of rainforest destruction.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: In other words, they gave no indication of an appreciation of either the range of ways in which rainforests are important or the complex social, economic and political factors which drive the activities which are destroying the rainforests.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: One encouragement is that the results of similar studies about other environmental issues suggest that older children seem to acquire the ability to appreciate, value and evaluate conflicting views.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 1
内容: Environmental education offers an arena in which these skills can be developed, which is essential for these children as future decision-makers.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Some of the senses that we and other terrestrial mammals take for granted are either reduced or absent in cetaceans or fail to function well in water.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: For example, it appears from their brain structure that toothed species are unable to smell.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Baleen species, on the other hand, appear to have some related brain structures but it is not known whether these are functional.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: It has been speculated that, as the blowholes evolved and migrated to the top of the head, the neural pathways serving sense of smell may have been nearly all sacrificed.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Similarly, although at least some cetaceans have taste buds, the nerves serving these have degenerated or are rudimentary.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The sense of touch has sometimes been described as weak too, but this view is probably mistaken.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Trainers of captive dolphins and small whales often remark on their animals' responsiveness to being touched or rubbed, and both captive and freeranging cetacean individuals of all species (particularly adults and calves, or members of the same subgroup) appear to make frequent contact.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: This contact may help to maintain order within a group, and stroking or touching are part of the courtship ritual in most species.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The area around the blowhole is also particularly sensitive and captive animals often object strongly to being touched there.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The sense of vision is developed to different degrees in different species.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Baleen species studied at close quarters underwater - specifically a grey whale calf in captivity for a year, and free-ranging right whales and humpback whales studied and filmed off Argentina and Hawaii - have obviously tracked objects with vision underwater, and they can apparently see moderately well both in water and in air.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: However, the position of the eyes so restricts the field of vision in baleen whales that they probably do not have stereoscopic vision.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: On the other hand, the position of the eyes in most dolphins and porpoises suggests that they have stereoscopic vision forward and downward.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Eye position in freshwater dolphins, which often swim on their side or upside down while feeding, suggests that what vision they have is stereoscopic forward and upward.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: By comparison, the bottlenose dolphin has extremely keen vision in water.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Judging from the way it watches and tracks airborne flying fish, it can apparently see fairly well through the air-water interface as well.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: And although preliminary experimental evidence suggests that their in-air vision is poor, the accuracy with which dolphins leap high to take small fish out of a trainer's hand provides anecdotal evidence to the contrary.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Such variation can no doubt be explained with reference to the habitats in which individual species have developed.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: For example, vision is obviously more useful to species inhabiting clear open waters than to those living in turbid rivers and flooded plains.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The South American boutu and Chinese beiji, for instance, appear to have very limited vision, and the Indian susus are blind, their eyes reduced to slits that probably allow them to sense only the direction and intensity of light.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Although the senses of taste and smell appear to have deteriorated, and vision in water appears to be uncertain, such weaknesses are more than compensated for by cetaceans' well-developed acoustic sense.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Most species are highly vocal, although they vary in the range of sounds they produce, and many forage for food using echolocation.

来源: IELTS4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Large baleen whales primarily use the lower frequencies and are often limited in their repertoire.

内容: It collects images from digital cameras running at 50 frames a second and breaks down each part of a swimmer's performance into factors that can be analysed individually - stroke length, stroke frequency, average duration of each stroke, velocity, start, lap and finish times, and so on.

内容: At the end of each race, SWAN spits out data on each swimmer.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Take a look, says Mason, pulling out a sheet of data.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: He points out the data on the swimmers in second and third place, which shows that the one who finished third actually swam faster.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: So why did he finish 35 hundredths of a second down?

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: 'His turn times were 44 hundredths of a second behind the other guy,' says Mason.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: 'If he can improve on his turns, he can do much better.'

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: This is the kind of accuracy that AIS scientists' research is bringing to a range of sports.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: With the Cooperative Research Centre for Micro Technology in Melbourne, they are developing unobtrusive sensors that will be embedded in an athlete's clothes or running shoes to monitor heart rate, sweating, heat production or any other factor that might have an impact on an athlete's ability to run.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: There's more to it than simply measuring performance.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Fricker gives the example of athletes who may be down with coughs and colds 11 or 12 times a year.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: After years of experimentation, AIS and the University of Newcastle in New South Wales developed a test that measures how much of the immune-system protein immunoglobulin A is present in athletes' saliva.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: If IgA levels suddenly fall below a certain level, training is eased or dropped altogether.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Soon, IgA levels start rising again, and the danger passes.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Since the tests were introduced, AIS athletes in all sports have been remarkably successful at staying healthy.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Using data is a complex business.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Well before a championship, sports scientists and coaches start to prepare the athlete by developing a 'competition model', based on what they expect will be the winning times.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: 'You design the model to make that time,' says Mason.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: 'A start of this much, each free-swimming period has to be this fast, with a certain stroke frequency and stroke length, with turns done in these times.'

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: All the training is then geared towards making the athlete hit those targets, both overall and for each segment of the race.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Techniques like these have transformed Australia into arguably the world's most successful sporting nation.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Of course, there's nothing to stop other countries copying - and many have tried.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some years ago, the AIS unveiled coolant-lined jackets for endurance athletes.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: At the Atlanta Olympic Games in 1996, these sliced as much as two per cent off cyclists' and rowers' times.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: Now everyone uses them.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: The same has happened to the 'altitude tent', developed by AIS to replicate the effect of altitude training at sea level.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 1
内容: But Australia's success story is about more than easily copied technological fixes, and up to now no nation has replicated its all-encompassing system.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: International trade is growing at a startling pace.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: While the global economy has been expanding at a bit over 3% a year, the volume of trade has been rising at a compound annual rate of about twice that.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Foreign products, from meat to machinery, play a more important role in almost every economy in the world, and foreign markets now tempt businesses that never much worried about sales beyond their nation's borders.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: What lies behind this explosion in international commerce?

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: The general worldwide decline in trade barriers, such as customs duties and import quotas, is surely one explanation.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: The economic opening of countries that have traditionally been minor players is another.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: But one force behind the import-export boom has passed all but unnoticed: the rapidly falling cost of getting goods to market.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Theoretically, in the world of trade, shipping costs do not matter.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Goods, once they have been made, are assumed to move instantly and at no cost from place to place.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: The real world, however, is full of frictions.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Cheap labour may make Chinese clothing competitive in America, but if delays in shipment tie up working capital and cause winter coats to arrive in spring, trade may lose its advantages.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: At the turn of the 20th century, agriculture and manufacturing were the two most important sectors almost everywhere, accounting for about 70% of total output in Germany, Italy and France, and 40 - 50% in America, Britain and Japan.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: International commerce was therefore dominated by raw materials, such as wheat, wood and iron ore, or processed commodities, such as meat and steel.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: But these sorts of products are heavy and bulky and the cost of transporting them relatively high.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Countries still trade disproportionately with their geographic neighbours.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Over time, however, world output has shifted into goods whose worth is unrelated to their size and weight.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Today, it is finished manufactured products that dominate the flow of trade, and, thanks to technological advances such as lightweight components, manufactured goods themselves have tended to become lighter and less bulky.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: As a result, less transportation is required for every dollar's worth of imports or exports.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: To see how this influences trade, consider the business of making disk drives for computers.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Most of the world's disk-drive manufacturing is concentrated in South-east Asia.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: This is possible only because disk drives, while valuable, are small and light and so cost little to ship.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Computer manufacturers in Japan or Texas will not face hugely bigger freight bills if they import drives from Singapore rather than purchasing them on the domestic market.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Distance therefore poses no obstacle to the globalisation of the disk-drive industry.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: This is even more true of the fast-growing information industries.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Films and compact discs cost little to transport, even by aeroplane.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Computer software can be 'exported' without ever loading it onto a ship, simply by transmitting it over telephone lines from one country to another, so freight rates and cargo-handling schedules become insignificant factors in deciding where to make the product.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Businesses can locate based on other considerations, such as the availability of labour, while worrying less about the cost of delivering their output.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: In many countries deregulation has helped to drive the process along.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: But, behind the scenes, a series of technological innovations known broadly as containerisation and inter-modal transportation has led to swift productivity improvements in cargo-handling.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Forty years ago, the process of exporting or importing involved a great many stages of handling, which risked portions of the shipment being damaged or stolen along the way.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: The invention of the container crane made it possible to load and unload containers without capsizing the ship and the adoption of standard container sizes allowed almost any box to be transported on any ship.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: By 1967, dual-purpose ships, carrying loose cargo in the hold and containers on the deck, were giving way to all-container vessels that moved thousands of boxes at a time.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: The shipping container transformed ocean shipping into a highly efficient, intensely competitive business.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: But getting the cargo to and from the dock was a different story.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: National governments, by and large, kept a much firmer hand on truck and railroad tariffs than on charges for ocean freight.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: This started changing, however, in the mid-1970s, when America began to deregulate its transportation industry.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: First airlines, then road hauliers and railways, were freed from restrictions on what they could carry, where they could haul it and what price they could charge.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Big productivity gains resulted.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Between 1985 and 1996, for example, America's freight railways dramatically reduced their employment, trackage, and their fleets of locomotives - while increasing the amount of cargo they hauled.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Europe's railways have also shown marked, albeit smaller, productivity improvements.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: In America the period of huge productivity gains in transportation may be almost over, but in most countries the process still has far to go.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: State ownership of railways and airlines, regulation of freight rates and toleration of anti-competitive practices, such as cargo-handling monopolies, all keep the cost of shipping unnecessarily high and deter international trade.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 2
内容: Bringing these barriers down would help the world's economies grow even closer.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Unusual incidents are being reported across the Arctic.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Inuit families going off on snowmobiles to prepare their summer hunting camps have found themselves cut off from home by a sea of mud, following early thaws.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: There are reports of igloos losing their insulating properties as the snow drips and refugees, of lakes draining into the sea as permafrost melts, and sea ice breaking up earlier than usual, carrying seals beyond the reach of hunters.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Climate change may still be a rather abstract idea to most of us, but in the Arctic it is already having dramatic effects - if summertime ice continues to shrink at its present rate, the Arctic Ocean could soon become virtually ice-free in summer.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: The knock-on effects are likely to include more warming, cloudier skies, increased precipitation and higher sea levels.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Scientists are increasingly keen to find out what's going on because they consider the Arctic the 'canary in the mine' for global warming - a warning of what's in store for the rest of the world.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: For the Inuit the problem is urgent.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: They live in precarious balance with one of the toughest environments on earth.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Climate change, whatever its causes, is a direct threat to their way of life.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Nobody knows the Arctic as well as the locals, which is why they are not content simply to stand back and let outside experts tell them what's happening.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: In Canada, where the Inuit people are jealously guarding their hard-won autonomy in the country's newest territory, Nunavut, they believe their best hope of survival in this changing environment lies in combining their ancestral knowledge with the best of modern science.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: This is a challenge in itself.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: The Canadian Arctic is a vast, treeless polar desert that's covered with snow for most of the year.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Venture into this terrain and you get some idea of the hardships facing anyone who calls this home.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Farming is out of the question and nature offers meagre pickings.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Humans first settled in the Arctic a mere 4,500 years ago, surviving by exploiting sea mammals and fish.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: The environment tested them to the limits: sometimes the colonists were successful, sometimes they failed and vanished.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: But around a thousand years ago, one group emerged that was uniquely well adapted to cope with the Arctic environment.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: These Thule people moved in from Alaska, bringing kayaks, sleds, dogs, pottery and iron tools.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: They are the ancestors of today's Inuit people.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Life for the descendants of the Thule people is still harsh.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Nunavut is 1.9 million square kilometres of rock and ice, and a handful of islands around the North Pole.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: It's currently home to 2,500 people, all but a handful of them indigenous Inuit.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Over the past 40 years, most have abandoned their nomadic ways and settled in the territory's 28 isolated communities, but they still rely heavily on nature to provide food and clothing.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Provisions available in local shops have to be flown into Nunavut on one of the most costly air networks in the world, or brought by supply ship during the few ice-free weeks of summer.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: It would cost a family around £7,000 a year to replace meat they obtained themselves through hunting with imported meat.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Economic opportunities are scarce, and for many people state benefits are their only income.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: While the Inuit may not actually starve if hunting and trapping are curtailed by climate change, there has certainly been an impact on people's health.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Obesity, heart disease and diabetes are beginning to appear in a people for whom these have never before been problems.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: There has been a crisis of identity as the traditional skills of hunting, trapping and preparing skins have begun to disappear.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: In Nunavut's 'igloo and email' society, where adults who were born in igloos have children who may never have been out on the land, there's a high incidence of depression.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: With so much at stake, the Inuit are determined to play a key role in teasing out the mysteries of climate change in the Arctic.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Having survived there for centuries, they believe their wealth of traditional knowledge is vital to the task.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: And Western scientists are starting to draw on this wisdom, increasingly referred to as 'Inuit Qaujimajatuqangit', or IQ.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: 'In the early days scientists ignored us when they came up here to study anything. They just figured these people don't know very much so we won't ask them,' says John Amagoalik, an Inuit leader and politician.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: 'But in recent years IQ has had much more credibility and weight.'

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: In fact it is now a requirement for anyone hoping to get permission to do research that they consult the communities, who are helping to set the research agenda to reflect their most important concerns.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: They can turn down applications from scientists they believe will work against their interests, or research projects that will impinge too much on their daily lives and traditional activities.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Some scientists doubt the value of traditional knowledge because the occupation of the Arctic doesn't go back far enough.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: Others, however, point out that the first weather stations in the far north date back just 50 years.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: There are still huge gaps in our environmental knowledge, and despite the scientific onslaught, many predictions are no more than best guesses.

来源: IELTS6 Test1 Reading Passage 3
内容: IQ could help to bridge the gap and resolve the tremendous uncertainty about how much of what we're seeing is natural capriciousness and how much is the consequence of human activity.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: A new study conducted for the World Bank by Murdoch University's Institute for Science and Technology Policy (ISTP) has demonstrated that public transport is more efficient than cars.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: The study compared the proportion of wealth poured into transport by thirty-seven cities around the world.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: This included both the public and private costs of building, maintaining and using a transport system.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: The study found that the Western Australian city of Perth is a good example of a city with minimal public transport.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: As a result, 17% of its wealth went into transport costs.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some European and Asian cities, on the other hand, spent as little as 5%.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Professor Peter Newman, ISTP Director, pointed out that these more efficient cities were able to put the difference into attracting industry and jobs or creating a better place to live.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: According to Professor Newman, the larger Australian city of Melbourne is a rather unusual city in this sort of comparison.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: He describes it as two cities: 'A European city surrounded by a car-dependent one'.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Melbourne's large tram network has made car use in the inner city much lower, but the outer suburbs have the same car-based structure as most other Australian cities.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: The explosion in demand for accommodation in the inner suburbs of Melbourne suggests a recent change in many people's preferences as to where they live.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Newman says this is a new, broader way of considering public transport issues.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: In the past, the case for public transport has been made on the basis of environmental and social justice considerations rather than economics.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Newman, however, believes the study demonstrates that 'the auto-dependent city model is inefficient and grossly inadequate in economic as well as environmental terms'.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Bicycle use was not included in the study but Newman noted that the two most 'bicycle friendly' cities considered - Amsterdam and Copenhagen - were very efficient, even though their public transport systems were 'reasonable but not special'.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: It is common for supporters of road networks to reject the models of cities with good public transport by arguing that such systems would not work in their particular city.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: One objection is climate.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some people say their city could not make more use of public transport because it is either too hot or too cold.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Newman rejects this, pointing out that public transport has been successful in both Toronto and Singapore and, in fact, he has checked the use of cars against climate and found 'zero correlation'.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: When it comes to other physical features, road lobbies are on stronger ground.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: For example, Newman accepts it would be hard for a city as hilly as Auckland to develop a really good rail network.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: However, he points out that both Hong Kong and Zurich have managed to make a success of their rail systems, heavy and light respectively, though there are few cities in the world as hilly.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: In fact, Newman believes the main reason for adopting one sort of transport over another is politics: 'The more democratic the process, the more public transport is favored.'

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: He considers Portland, Oregon, a perfect example of this.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Some years ago, federal money was granted to build a new road.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: However, local pressure groups forced a referendum over whether to spend the money on light rail instead.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: The rail proposal won and the railway worked spectacularly well.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: In the years that have followed, more and more rail systems have been put in, dramatically changing the nature of the city.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Newman notes that Portland has about the same population as Perth and had a similar population density at the time.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: In the UK, travel times to work had been stable for at least six centuries, with people avoiding situations that required them to spend more than half an hour travelling to work.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Trains and cars initially allowed people to live at greater distances without taking longer to reach their destination.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: However, public infrastructure did not keep pace with urban sprawl, causing massive congestion problems which now make commuting times far higher.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: There is a widespread belief that increasing wealth encourages people to live farther out where cars are the only viable transport.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: The example of European cities refutes that.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: They are often wealthier than their American counterparts but have not generated the same level of car use.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: In Stockholm, car use has actually fallen in recent years as the city has become larger and wealthier.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: A new study makes this point even more starkly.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Developing cities in Asia, such as Jakarta and Bangkok, make more use of the car than wealthy Asian cities such as Tokyo and Singapore.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: In cities that developed later, the World Bank and Asian Development Bank discouraged the building of public transport and people have been forced to rely on cars - creating the massive traffic jams that characterize those cities.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Newman believes one of the best studies on how cities built for cars might be converted to rail use is The Urban Village report, which used Melbourne as an example.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: It found that pushing everyone into the city centre was not the best approach.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: Instead, the proposal advocated the creation of urban villages at hundreds of sites, mostly around railway stations.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: It was once assumed that improvements in telecommunications would lead to more dispersal in the population as people were no longer forced into cities.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: However, the ISTP team's research demonstrates that the population and job density of cities rose or remained constant in the 1980s after decades of decline.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: The explanation for this seems to be that it is valuable to place people working in related fields together.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 1
内容: 'The new world will largely depend on human creativity, and creativity flourishes where people come together face-to-face.'

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Elderly people are growing healthier, happier and more independent, say American scientists.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: The results of a 14-year study to be announced later this month reveal that the diseases associated with old age are afflicting fewer and fewer people and when they do strike, it is much later in life.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: In the last 14 years, the National Long-term Health Care Survey has gathered data on the health and lifestyles of more than 20,000 men and women over 65.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Researchers, now analysing the results of data gathered in 1994, say arthritis, high blood pressure and circulation problems - the major medical complaints in this age group - are troubling a smaller proportion every year.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: And the data confirms that the rate at which these diseases are declining continues to accelerate.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Other diseases of old age - dementia, stroke, arteriosclerosis and emphysema - are also troubling fewer and fewer people.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'It really raises the question of what should be considered normal ageing,' says Kenneth Manton, a demographer from Duke University in North Carolina.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: He says the problems doctors accepted as normal in a 65-year-old in 1982 are often not appearing until people are 70 or 75.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Clearly, certain diseases are beating a retreat in the face of medical advances.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: But there may be other contributing factors.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Improvements in childhood nutrition in the first quarter of the twentieth century, for example, gave today's elderly people a better start in life than their predecessors.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: On the downside, the data also reveals failures in public health that have caused surges in some illnesses.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: An increase in some cancers and bronchitis may reflect changing smoking habits and poorer air quality, say the researchers.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'These may be subtle influences,' says Manton, 'but our subjects have been exposed to worse and worse pollution for over 60 years. It's not surprising we see some effect.'

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: One interesting correlation Manton uncovered is that better-educated people are likely to live longer.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: For example, 65-year-old women with fewer than eight years of schooling are expected, on average, to live to 82.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Those who continued their education live an extra seven years.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Although some of this can be attributed to a higher income, Manton believes it is mainly because educated people seek more medical attention.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: The survey also assessed how independent people over 65 were, and again found a striking trend.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Almost 80% of those in the 1994 survey could complete everyday activities ranging from eating and dressing unaided to complex tasks such as cooking and managing their finances.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: That represents a significant drop in the number of disabled old people in the population.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: If the trends apparent in the United States 14 years ago had continued, researchers calculate there would be an additional one million disabled elderly people in today's population.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: According to Manton, slowing the trend has saved the United States government's Medicare system more than $200 billion, suggesting that the greying of America's population may prove less of a financial burden than expected.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: The increasing self-reliance of many elderly people is probably linked to a massive increase in the use of simple home medical aids.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: For instance, the use of raised toilet seats has more than doubled since the start of the study, and the use of bath seats has grown by more than 50%.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: These developments also bring some health benefits, according to a report from the MacArthur Foundation's research group on successful ageing.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: The group found that those elderly people who were able to retain a sense of independence were more likely to stay healthy in old age.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Maintaining a level of daily physical activity may help mental functioning, says Carl Cotman, a neuroscientist at the University of California at Irvine.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: He found that rats that exercise on a treadmill have raised levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor coursing through their brains.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Cotman believes this hormone, which keeps neurons functioning, may prevent the brains of active humans from deteriorating.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: As part of the same study, Teresa Seeman, a social epidemiologist at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, found a connection between self-esteem and stress in people over 70.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: In laboratory simulations of challenging activities such as driving, those who felt in control of their lives pumped out lower levels of stress hormones such as cortisol.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Chronically high levels of these hormones have been linked to heart disease.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: But independence can have drawbacks.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: Seeman found that elderly people who felt emotionally isolated maintained higher levels of stress hormones even when asleep.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: The research suggests that older people fare best when they feel independent but know they can get help when they need it.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'Like much research into ageing, these results support common sense,' says Seeman.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: They also show that we may be underestimating the impact of these simple factors.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'The sort of thing that your grandmother always told you turns out to be right on target,' she says.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: One of the first great intellectual feats of a young child is learning how to talk, closely followed by learning how to count.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: From earliest childhood we are so bound up with our system of numeration that it is a feat of imagination to consider the problems faced by early humans who had not yet developed this facility.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Careful consideration of our system of numeration leads to the conviction that, rather than being a facility that comes naturally to a person, it is one of the great and remarkable achievements of the human race.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: It is impossible to learn the sequence of events that led to our developing the concept of number.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Even the earliest of tribes had a system of numeration that, if not advanced, was sufficient for the tasks that they had to perform.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Our ancestors had little use for actual numbers; instead their considerations would have been more of the kind 'Is this enough?' rather than 'How many?' when they were engaged in food gathering, for example.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: However, when early humans first began to reflect on the nature of things around them, they discovered that they needed an idea of number simply to keep their thoughts in order.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: As they began to settle, grow plants and herd animals, the need for a sophisticated number system became paramount.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: It will never be known how and when this numeration ability developed, but it is certain that numeration was well developed by the time humans had formed even semi-permanent settlements.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Evidence of early stages of arithmetic and numeration can be readily found.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: The indigenous peoples of Tasmania were only able to count one, two, many; those of South Africa counted one, two, two and one, two twos, two twos and one, and so on.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: But in real situations the number and words are often accompanied by gestures to help resolve any confusion.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: For example, when using the one, two, many type of system, the word 'many' would mean, 'look at my hands and see how many fingers I am showing you'.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: This basic approach is limited in the range of numbers that it can express, but this range will generally suffice when dealing with the simpler aspects of human existence.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: The lack of ability of some cultures to deal with large numbers is not really surprising.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: European languages, when traced back to their earlier version, are very poor in number words and expressions.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: The ancient Gothic word for ten, tachund, is used to express the number 100 as tachund tachund.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: By the seventh century, the word teon had become interchangeable with the tachund or hund of the Anglo-Saxon language, and so 100 was denoted as hund teontig, or ten times ten.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: The average person in the seventh century in Europe was not as familiar with numbers as we are today.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: In fact, to qualify as a witness in a court of law a man had to be able to count to nine!

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Perhaps the most fundamental step in developing a sense of number is not the ability to count, but rather to see that a number is really an abstract idea instead of a simple attachment to a group of particular objects.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: It must have been within the grasp of the earliest humans to conceive that four birds are distinct from two birds; however, it is not an elementary step to associate the number 4, as connected with four birds, to the number 4, as connected with four rocks.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Associating a number as one of the qualities of a specific object is a great hindrance to the development of a true number sense.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: When the number 4 can be registered in the mind as a specific word, independent of the object being referenced, the individual is ready to take the first step toward the development of a notational system for numbers and, from there, to arithmetic.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Traces of the very first stages in the development of numeration can be seen in several living languages today.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: The numeration system of the Tsimshian language in British Columbia contains seven distinct sets of words for numbers according to the class of the item being counted: for counting flat objects and animals, for round objects and time, for people, for long objects and trees, for canoes, for measures, and for counting when no particular object is being numerated.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: It seems that the last is a later development while the first six groups show the relics of an older system.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: This diversity of number names can also be found in some widely used languages such as Japanese.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Intermixed with the development of a number sense is the development of an ability to count.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Counting is not directly related to the formation of a number concept because it is possible to count by matching the items being counted against a group of pebbles, grains of corn, or the counter's fingers.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: These aids would have been indispensable to very early people who would have found the process impossible without some form of mechanical aid.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: Such aids, while different, are still used even by the most educated in today's society due to their convenience.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: All counting ultimately involves reference to something other than the things being counted.

来源: IELTS6 Test2 Reading Passage 3
内容: At first it may have been grains or pebbles but now it is a memorised sequence of words that happen to be the names of the numbers.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: The Lumière Brothers opened their Cinematographe, at 14 Boulevard des Capucines in Paris, to 100 paying customers over 100 years ago, on December 8, 1895.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Before the eyes of the stunned, thrilled audience, photographs came to life and moved across a flat screen.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: So ordinary and routine has this become to us that it takes a determined leap of the imagination to grasp the impact of those first moving images.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: But it is worth trying, for to understand the initial shock of those images is to understand the extraordinary power and magic of cinema, the unique, hypnotic quality that has made film the most dynamic, effective art form of the 20th century.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: One of the Lumière Brothers' earliest films was a 30-second piece which showed a section of a railway platform flooded with sunshine.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: A train appears and heads straight for the camera.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: And that is all that happens.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Yet the Russian director Andrei Tarkovsky, one of the greatest of all film artists, described the film as a 'work of genius'.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: 'As the train approached,' wrote Tarkovsky, 'panic started in the theatre: people jumped and ran away. That was the moment when cinema was born. The frightened audience could not accept that they were watching a mere picture. Pictures were still, only reality moved; this must, therefore, be reality. In their confusion, they feared that a real train was about to crush them.'

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Early cinema audiences often experienced the same confusion.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: In time, the idea of film became familiar, the magic was accepted - but it never stopped being magic.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Film has never lost its unique power to embrace its audiences and transport them to a different world.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: For Tarkovsky, the key to that magic was the way in which cinema created a dynamic image of the real flow of events.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: A still picture could only imply the existence of time, while time in a novel passed at the whim of the reader.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: But in cinema, the real, objective flow of time was captured.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: One effect of this realism was to educate the world about itself.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: For cinema makes the world smaller.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Long before people travelled to America or anywhere else, they knew what other places looked like; they knew how other people worked and lived.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Overwhelmingly, the lives recorded - at least in film fiction - have been American.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: From the earliest days of the industry, Hollywood has dominated the world film market.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: American imagery - the cars, the cities, the cowboys - became the primary imagery of film.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Film carried American life and values around the globe.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: And, thanks to film, future generations will know the 20th century more intimately than any other period.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: We can only imagine what life was like in the 14th century or in classical Greece.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: But the life of the modern world has been recorded on film in massive, encyclopaedic detail.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: We shall be known better than any preceding generations.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: The 'star' was another natural consequence of cinema.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: The cinema star was effectively born in 1910.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Film personalities have such an immediate presence that, inevitably, they become super-real.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Because we watch them so closely and because everybody in the world seems to know who they are, they appear more real to us than we do ourselves.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: The star as magnified human self is one of cinema's most strange and enduring legacies.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Cinema has also given a new lease of life to the idea of the story.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: When the Lumière Brothers and other pioneers began showing off this new invention, it was by no means obvious how it would be used.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: All that mattered at first was the wonder of movement.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Indeed, some said that, once this novelty had worn off, cinema would fade away.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: It was no more than a passing gimmick, a fairground attraction.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Cinema might, for example, have become primarily a documentary form.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Or it might have developed like television - as a strange, noisy transfer of music, information and narrative.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: But what happened was that it became, overwhelmingly, a medium for telling stories.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Originally these were conceived as short stories - early producers doubted the ability of audiences to concentrate for more than the length of a reel.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Then, in 1912, an Italian 2-hour film was hugely successful, and Hollywood settled upon the novel-length narrative that remains the dominant cinematic convention of today.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: And it has all happened so quickly.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 1
内容: Almost unbelievably, it is a mere 100 years since that train arrived and the audience screamed and fled, convinced by the dangerous reality of what they saw, and, perhaps, suddenly aware that the world could never be the same again - that, maybe, it could be better, brighter, more astonishing, more real than reality.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: It is a great deal easier to motivate employees in a growing organisation than a declining one.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: When organisations are expanding and adding personnel, promotional opportunities, pay rises, and the excitement of being associated with a dynamic organisation create feelings of optimism.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Management is able to use the growth to entice and encourage employees.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: When an organisation is shrinking, the best and most mobile workers are prone to leave voluntarily.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Unfortunately, they are the ones the organisation can least afford to lose - those with the highest skills and experience.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The minor employees remain because their job options are limited.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Morale also suffers during decline.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: People fear they may be the next to be made redundant.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Productivity often suffers, as employees spend their time sharing rumours and providing one another with moral support rather than focusing on their jobs.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: For those whose jobs are secure, pay increases are rarely possible.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Pay cuts, unheard of during times of growth, may even be imposed.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The challenge to management is how to motivate employees under such retrenchment conditions.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The ways of meeting this challenge can be broadly divided into six Key Points, which are outlined below.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: There is an abundance of evidence to support the motivational benefits that result from carefully matching people to jobs.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: For example, if the job is running a small business or an autonomous unit within a larger business, high achievers should be sought.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: However, if the job to be filled is a managerial post in a large bureaucratic organisation, a candidate who has a high need for power and a low need for affiliation should be selected.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Accordingly, high achievers should not be put into jobs that are inconsistent with their needs.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: High achievers will do best when the job provides moderately challenging goals and where there is independence and feedback.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: However, it should be remembered that not everybody is motivated by jobs that are high in independence, variety and responsibility.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The literature on goal-setting theory suggests that managers should ensure that all employees have specific goals and receive comments on how well they are doing in those goals.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: For those with high achievement needs, typically a minority in any organisation, the existence of external goals is less important because high achievers are already internally motivated.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The next factor to be determined is whether the goals should be assigned by a manager or collectively set in conjunction with the employees.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The answer to that depends on perceptions of goal acceptance and the organisation's culture.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: If resistance to goals is expected, the use of participation in goal-setting should increase acceptance.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: If participation is inconsistent with the culture, however, goals should be assigned.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: If participation and the culture are incongruous, employees are likely to perceive the participation process as manipulative and be negatively affected by it.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Regardless of whether goals are achievable or well within management's perceptions of the employee's ability, if employees see them as unachievable they will reduce their effort.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Managers must be sure, therefore, that employees feel confident that their efforts can lead to performance goals.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: For managers, this means that employees must have the capability of doing the job and must regard the appraisal process as valid.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Since employees have different needs, what acts as a reinforcement for one may not for another.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Managers could use their knowledge of each employee to personalise the rewards over which they have control.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Some of the more obvious rewards that managers allocate include pay, promotions, autonomy, job scope and depth, and the opportunity to participate in goal-setting and decision-making.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Managers need to make rewards contingent on performance.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: To reward factors other than performance will only reinforce those other factors.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Key rewards such as pay increases and promotions or advancements should be allocated for the attainment of the employee's specific goals.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Consistent with maximising the impact of rewards, managers should look for ways to increase their visibility.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Eliminating the secrecy surrounding pay by openly communicating everyone's remuneration, publicising performance bonuses and allocating annual salary increases in a lump sum rather than spreading them out over an entire year are examples of actions that will make rewards more visible and potentially more motivating.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The way rewards are distributed should be transparent so that employees perceive that rewards or outcomes are equitable and equal to the inputs given.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: On a simplistic level, experience, abilities, effort and other obvious inputs should explain differences in pay, responsibility and other obvious outcomes.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The problem, however, is complicated by the existence of dozens of inputs and outcomes and by the fact that employee groups place different degrees of importance on them.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: For instance, a study comparing clerical and production workers identified nearly twenty inputs and outcomes.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: The clerical workers considered factors such as quality of work performed and job knowledge near the top of their list, but these were at the bottom of the production workers' list.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Similarly, production workers thought that the most important inputs were intelligence and personal involvement with task accomplishment, two factors that were quite low in the importance ratings of the clerks.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: There were also important, though less dramatic, differences on the outcome side.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: For example, production workers rated advancement very highly, whereas clerical workers rated advancement in the lower third of their list.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 2
内容: Such findings suggest that one person's equity is another's inequity, so an ideal should probably weigh different inputs and outcomes according to employee group.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: As researchers on aging noted recently, no treatment on the market today has been proved to slow human aging - the build-up of molecular and cellular damage that increases vulnerability to infirmity as we grow older.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: But one intervention, consumption of a low-calorie yet nutritionally balanced diet, works incredibly well in a broad range of animals, increasing longevity and prolonging good health.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Those findings suggest that caloric restriction could delay aging and increase longevity in humans, too.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Unfortunately, for maximum benefit, people would probably have to reduce their caloric intake by roughly thirty per cent, equivalent to dropping from 2,500 calories a day to 1,750.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Few mortals could stick to that harsh a regimen, especially for years on end.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: But what if someone could create a pill that mimicked the physiological effects of eating less without actually forcing people to eat less?

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Could such a 'caloric-restriction mimetic', as we call it, enable people to stay healthy longer, postponing age-related disorders (such as diabetes, arteriosclerosis, heart disease and cancer) until very late in life?

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Scientists first posed this question in the mid-1990s, after researchers came upon a chemical agent that in rodents seemed to reproduce many of caloric restriction's benefits.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: No compound that would safely achieve the same feat in people has been found yet, but the search has been informative and has fanned hope that caloric-restriction (CR) mimetics can indeed be developed eventually.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: The hunt for CR mimetics grew out of a desire to better understand caloric restriction's many effects on the body.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Scientists first recognized the value of the practice more than 60 years ago, when they found that rats fed a low-calorie diet lived longer on average than free-feeding rats and also had a reduced incidence of conditions that become increasingly common in old age.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: What is more, some of the treated animals survived longer than the oldest-living animals in the control group, which means that the maximum lifespan (the oldest attainable age), not merely the normal lifespan, increased.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Various interventions, such as infection-fighting drugs, can increase a population's average survival time, but only approaches that slow the body's rate of aging will increase the maximum lifespan.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: The rat findings have been replicated many times and extended to creatures ranging from yeast to fruit flies, worms, fish, spiders, mice and hamsters.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Until fairly recently, the studies were limited to short-lived creatures genetically distant from humans.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: But caloric-restriction projects underway in two species more closely related to humans - rhesus and squirrel monkeys - have made scientists optimistic that CR mimetics could help people.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: The monkey projects demonstrate that, compared with control animals that eat normally, caloric-restricted monkeys have lower body temperatures and levels of the pancreatic hormone insulin, and they retain more youthful levels of certain hormones that tend to fall with age.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: The caloric-restricted animals also look better on indicators of risk for age-related diseases.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: For example, they have lower blood pressure and triglyceride levels (signifying a decreased likelihood of heart disease), and they have more normal blood glucose levels (pointing to a reduced risk for diabetes, which is marked by unusually high blood glucose levels).

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Further, it has recently been shown that rhesus monkeys kept on caloric-restricted diets for an extended time (nearly 15 years) have less chronic disease.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: They and the other monkeys must be followed still longer, however, to know whether low-calorie intake can increase both average and maximum lifespans in monkeys.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Unlike the multitude of elixirs being touted as the latest anti-aging cure, CR mimetics would alter fundamental processes that underlie aging.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: We aim to develop compounds that fool cells into activating maintenance and repair.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: The best-studied candidate for a caloric-restriction mimetic, 2DG (2-deoxy-D-glucose), works by interfering with the way cells process glucose.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: It has proved toxic at some doses in animals and so cannot be used in humans.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: But it has demonstrated that chemicals can replicate the effects of caloric restriction; the trick is finding the right one.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Cells use the glucose from food to generate ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the molecule that powers many activities in the body.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: By limiting food intake, caloric restriction minimizes the amount of glucose entering cells and decreases ATP generation.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: When 2DG is administered to animals that eat normally, glucose reaches cells in abundance but the drug prevents most of it from being processed and thus reduces ATP synthesis.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Researchers have proposed several explanations for why interruption of glucose processing and ATP production might retard aging.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: One possibility relates to the ATP-making machinery's emission of free radicals, which are thought to contribute to aging and to such age-related diseases as cancer by damaging cells.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Reduced operation of the machinery should limit their production and thereby constrain the damage.

来源: IELTS6 Test3 Reading Passage 3
内容: Another hypothesis suggests that decreased processing of glucose could indicate to cells that food is scarce (even if it isn't) and induce them to shift into an anti-aging mode that emphasizes preservation of the organism over such 'luxuries' as growth and reproduction.

内容: 'It's a very profitable industry.'
