来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Children in developing countries are healthier and more likely to survive past the age of five when their mothers can read and write.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Experts in public health accepted this idea decades ago, but until now no one has been able to show that a woman's ability to read in itself improves her children's chances of survival.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Most literate women learnt to read in primary school, and the fact that a woman has had an education may simply indicate her family's wealth or that it values its children more highly.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Now a long-term study carried out in Nicaragua has eliminated these factors by showing that teaching reading to poor adult women, who would otherwise have remained illiterate, has a direct effect on their children's health and survival.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: In 1979, the government of Nicaragua established a number of social programmes, including a National Literacy Crusade.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: By 1985, about 300,000 illiterate adults from all over the country, many of whom had never attended primary school, had learnt how to read, write and use numbers.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: During this period, researchers from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, the Central American Institute of Health in Nicaragua, the National Autonomous University of Nicaragua and the Costa Rican Institute of Health interviewed nearly 3,000 women, some of whom had learnt to read as children, some during the literacy crusade and some who had never learnt at all.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The women were asked how many children they had given birth to and how many of them had died in infancy.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The research teams also examined the surviving children to find out how well-nourished they were.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The investigators' findings were striking.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: In the late 1970s, the infant mortality rate for the children of illiterate mothers was around 110 deaths per thousand live births.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: At this point in their lives, those mothers who later went on to learn to read had a similar level of child mortality (105/1000).

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: For women educated in primary school, however, the infant mortality rate was significantly lower, at 80 per thousand.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: In 1985, after the National Literacy Crusade had ended, the infant mortality figures for those who remained illiterate and for those educated in primary school remained more or less unchanged.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: For those women who learnt to read through the campaign, the infant mortality rate was 84 per thousand, an impressive 21 points lower than for those women who were still illiterate.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The children of the newly-literate mothers were also better nourished than those of women who could not read.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Why are the children of literate mothers better off?

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: According to Peter Sandiford of the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, no one knows for certain.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Child health was not on the curriculum during the women's lessons, so he and his colleagues are looking at other factors.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: They are working with the same group of 3,000 women, to try to find out whether reading mothers make better use of hospitals and clinics, opt for smaller families, exert more control at home, learn modern childcare techniques more quickly, or whether they merely have more respect for themselves and their children.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The Nicaraguan study may have important implications for governments and aid agencies that need to know where to direct their resources.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Sandiford says that there is increasing evidence that female education, at any age, is 'an important health intervention in its own right'.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: The results of the study lend support to the World Bank's recommendation that education budgets in developing countries should be increased, not just to help their economies, but also to improve child health.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'We've known for a long time that maternal education is important,' says John Cleland of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'But we thought that even if we started educating girls today, we'd have to wait a generation for the pay-off. The Nicaraguan study suggests we may be able to bypass that.'

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Cleland warns that the Nicaraguan crusade was special in many ways, and similar campaigns elsewhere might not work as well.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: It is notoriously difficult to teach adults skills that do not have an immediate impact on their everyday lives, and many literacy campaigns in other countries have been much less successful.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: 'The crusade was part of a larger effort to bring a better life to the people,' says Cleland.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 2
内容: Replicating these conditions in other countries will be a major challenge for development workers.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Persistent bullying is one of the worst experiences a child can face.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: How can it be prevented?

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Peter Smith, Professor of Psychology at the University of Sheffield, directed the Sheffield Anti-Bullying Intervention Project, funded by the Department for Education.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Here he reports on his findings.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Bullying can take a variety of forms, from the verbal - being taunted or called hurtful names - to the physical - being kicked or shoved - as well as indirect forms, such as being excluded from social groups.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: A survey I conducted with Irene Whitney found that in British primary schools up to a quarter of pupils reported experience of bullying, which in about one in ten cases was persistent.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: There was less bullying in secondary schools, with about one in twenty-five suffering persistent bullying, but these cases may be particularly recalcitrant.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Bullying is clearly unpleasant, and can make the child experiencing it feel unworthy and depressed.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: In extreme cases it can even lead to suicide, though this is thankfully rare.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Victimised pupils are more likely to experience difficulties with interpersonal relationships as adults, while children who persistently bully are more likely to grow up to be physically violent, and convicted of anti-social offences.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Until recently, not much was known about the topic, and little help was available to teachers to deal with bullying.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Perhaps as a consequence, schools would often deny the problem.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: 'There is no bullying at this school' has been a common refrain, almost certainly untrue.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Fortunately more schools are now saying: 'There is not much bullying here, but when it occurs we have a clear policy for dealing with it.'

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Three factors are involved in this change.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: First is an awareness of the severity of the problem.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Second, a number of resources to help tackle bullying have become available in Britain.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: For example, the Scottish Council for Research in Education produced a package of materials, Action Against Bullying, circulated to all schools in England and Wales as well as in Scotland in summer 1992, with a second pack, Supporting Schools Against Bullying, produced the following year.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: In Ireland, Guidelines on Countering Bullying Behaviour in Post-Primary Schools was published in 1993.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Third, there is evidence that these materials work, and that schools can achieve something.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: This comes from carefully conducted 'before and after' evaluations of interventions in schools, monitored by a research team.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: In Norway, after an intervention campaign was introduced nationally, an evaluation of forty-two schools suggested that, over a two-year period, bullying was halved.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: The Sheffield investigation, which involved sixteen primary schools and seven secondary schools, found that most schools succeeded in reducing bullying.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Evidence suggests that a key step is to develop a policy on bullying, saying clearly what is meant by bullying, and giving explicit guidelines on what will be done if it occurs, what records will be kept, who will be informed, what sanctions will be employed.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: The policy should be developed through consultation, over a period of time - not just imposed from the head teacher's office!

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Pupils, parents and staff should feel they have been involved in the policy, which needs to be disseminated and implemented effectively.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Other actions can be taken to back up the policy.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: There are ways of dealing with the topic through the curriculum, using video, drama and literature.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: These are useful for raising awareness, and can best be tied in to early phases of development, while the school is starting to discuss the issue of bullying.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: They are also useful in renewing the policy for new pupils, or revising it in the light of experience.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: But curriculum work alone may only have short-term effects; it should be an addition to policy work, not a substitute.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: There are also ways of working with individual pupils, or in small groups.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Assertiveness training for pupils who are liable to be victims is worthwhile, and certain approaches to group bullying such as 'no blame', can be useful in changing the behaviour of bullying pupils without confronting them directly, although other sanctions may be needed for those who continue with persistent bullying.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Work in the playground is important, too.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: One helpful step is to train lunchtime supervisors to distinguish bullying from playful fighting, and help them break up conflicts.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: Another possibility is to improve the playground environment, so that pupils are less likely to be led into bullying from boredom or frustration.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: With these developments, schools can expect that at least the most serious kinds of bullying can largely be prevented.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: The more effort put in and the wider the whole school involvement, the more substantial the results are likely to be.

来源: IELTS6 Test4 Reading Passage 3
内容: The reduction in bullying - and the consequent improvement in pupil happiness - is surely a worthwhile objective.
